stats.label: When your 8 o'clock crew actually pulls up
Surprise line items on the final bill
Door to door, for most local moves

services.title: Full-service local moves
services.desc: We bring the truck, the pads, the dollies and the crew. You point at things; they end up in the right room across town.

services.title: Loading & unloading only
services.desc: Renting your own truck or loading a storage container? A crew meets you on either end and does the heavy part right.

services.title: In-house moves
services.desc: New flooring, a nursery swap, a piano that needs to be downstairs — we move furniture within your home, padded and unhurried.

services.title: Packing add-on
services.desc: A packing crew the day before: boxes, paper and wrap included, kitchens and closets boxed and labeled so moving day starts at zero.

crewTiers.label: 4 movers + truck
crewTiers.fit: Big houses, stairs everywhere, short timelines

loadNote: These are honest ballparks, not quotes — stairs, long carries and how tightly the boxes are packed all move the number. The walkthrough pins it down.

process.title: The walkthrough
process.desc: Fifteen minutes, in person or over video. We see what's moving, flag the heavy stuff, and give you a number you can hold us to.

process.title: Protect first
process.desc: Floor runners down, door frames and stair rails padded before the first box moves. Your house gets wrapped, not just your furniture.

process.title: The load plan
process.desc: Heavy low, fragile last-on-first-off, every strap where the crew lead calls it. A tight load is a safe load.

process.title: Set down & settle
process.desc: Beds rebuilt, sofa where you want it, boxes to their labeled rooms. We're not done until you've walked the empty truck.

billableNote: The clock starts when the truck pulls up and stops when you tell us we're done. Travel inside the valley is built into the rate — you don't pay us to drive to you.
pricingNote: Rates are straight hourly — no fuel surcharges, no stair fees, no heavy-item ambush on the final bill. Pianos and safes just need a heads-up at the walkthrough so the right rigging is on the truck.

owner.name: Boone Latimer
owner.heading: The rule from the loading dock
owner.bio: Boone Latimer spent his summers loading produce trucks in the warehouse district, where a sloppy pallet meant somebody ate the loss. He started Osprey Moving Co. with one truck and the rule he learned on the dock: load it like it's yours, set it down like it's your grandmother's. Most of the crew came off those same docks — people who treat a tight load as a point of pride, not a chore.

faq.q: Do I have to empty every drawer?
faq.a: Light, soft stuff — clothes, linens — can usually stay in dressers; we wrap and move the whole piece. Anything that rattles, leaks or breaks comes out. When in doubt, ask at the walkthrough.

No — we stay local on purpose. If you're headed beyond the valley, we'll gladly load your rental truck or container and point you to a long-haul carrier for the road part. We'd rather be great inside the valley than mediocre across three states.

Uprights, yes — with the board, the straps and enough hands, planned at the walkthrough. Grands and player pianos want a specialty rig, and we'll say so honestly instead of improvising with your instrument.

Propane tanks, gas cans with gas still in them, open liquids, and anything alive except your houseplants — those ride in your car, where the temperature is kinder. The crew lead flags anything else at the walkthrough, not on moving day.
Tell the crew lead before the truck leaves and we make it right — that's the whole policy. Pieces you'd hate to lose get named at the walkthrough, wrapped first, and carried by the lead personally.

faq.q: How far ahead should I book?
faq.a: Two to three weeks for month-end and summer weekends; mid-month weekdays are often days away. In a genuine pinch, call — a small crew can sometimes slot a small move inside the week.
